lem-ip-collared-sobolev-besov-source-fun:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Put $\Omega=B_1(0)\subset\mathbb R^3$, fix $0<\rho<1$, and let $5/2<s<7/2$ and $s<t<2s-1$. Use the following precise intrinsic Hilbert norm on $H^s(\Omega)$. If $s=m+\theta$ with integer $m\ge0$ and $0<\theta<1$, set
$$\|v\|_{s,\Omega}^2=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m}\|D^\alpha v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{|\alpha|=m}\int_{\Omega\times\Omega}\frac{|D^\alpha v(x)-D^\alpha v(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{3+2\theta}}\,dx\,dy.$$
For integer $s=3$ use just the derivative sum with $m=3$. Denote the corresponding real inner product by $(\cdot,\cdot)_{s,\Omega}$. On $\mathbb R^3$ use the unitary Fourier transform and $\|f\|_{H^r}^2=\int\langle\xi\rangle^{2r}|\widehat f(\xi)|^2d\xi$. Let $B^r_{2,\infty}(\mathbb R^3)$ have norm $\sup_{j\ge0}2^{jr}\|\mathbf1_{A_j}\widehat f\|_2$, where $A_0=\{|\xi|<2\}$ and $A_j=\{2^j\le|\xi|<2^{j+1}\}$ for $j\ge1$; the restriction space on $\Omega$ consists of restrictions of members of this whole-space Besov space.

Let $\sigma^\dagger\in H^s(\Omega)\cap B^t_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ be real and equal to $1$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus B_\rho$. Then there is $C>0$, depending on $\sigma^\dagger,s,t,\rho$, such that for every real $\sigma\in H^s(\Omega)$ also equal to $1$ there and every integer $J\ge0$,
$$-(\sigma^\dagger,\sigma-\sigma^\dagger)_{s,\Omega}\le C2^{J(2s-t-1)}\|\sigma-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^1(\Omega)}+C2^{-J(t-s)}\|\sigma-\sigma^\dagger\|_{s,\Omega}.$$
Consequently, suppose on a specified admissible sublevel a forward map $G$ satisfies $\|\sigma-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_0\omega(\|G(\sigma)-G(\sigma^\dagger)\|)$ with $\omega(0)=0$ and $0\le\omega\le1$. For the exact regularizer $R(\sigma)=\frac12\|\sigma\|_{s,\Omega}^2$, its exact Bregman distance is $D_R(\sigma,\sigma^\dagger)=\frac12\|\sigma-\sigma^\dagger\|_{s,\Omega}^2$, and
$$-(\sigma^\dagger,\sigma-\sigma^\dagger)_{s,\Omega}\le\frac34D_R(\sigma,\sigma^\dagger)+C_1\omega(\|G(\sigma)-G(\sigma^\dagger)\|)^{2(t-s)/(t-1)}.$$
In particular, an $H^1$ stability modulus of order $[\log(1/u)]^{-(s-3/2)}$ yields a VSC source term of order $[\log(1/u)]^{-\nu}$ with $\nu=(t-s)(2s-3)/(t-1)$. The conditional stability estimate is a hypothesis here, not a conclusion.
lem-ip-positive-sobolev-cgo-remainders-b:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $0<\tau<1$, $0<\rho<1$ and $M>0$. If $q\in H^{1/2+\tau}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ has support in $\overline{B_\rho}$ and norm at most $M$, there are constants $T,C>0$, depending only on $\tau,\rho,M$, such that for every $\zeta\in\mathbb C^3$ with $\zeta\cdot\zeta=0$ and $|\zeta|\ge T$, there is $r_\zeta\in H^2(B_2)$ for which
$$(-\Delta+q)\big(e^{i\zeta\cdot x}(1+r_\zeta)\big)=0\quad\hbox{in }B_2,$$
$$\|r_\zeta\|_{H^{1/2}(B_2)}\le C|\zeta|^{-1}M,\qquad \|r_\zeta\|_{L^\infty(B_2)}\le C|\zeta|^{-\tau/2}M,\qquad \|r_\zeta\|_{H^2(B_2)}\le C|\zeta|M(1+M).$$
Here fractional Sobolev norms on the ball are restriction norms from the whole-space Fourier Sobolev spaces. No boundary condition is imposed. The construction is on a larger cube, so the stated regularity holds on a neighborhood of the closed unit ball.
lem-ip-sharp-weighted-modulated-cgo-rema:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Write $\langle\xi\rangle=(1+|\xi|^2)^{1/2}$ and use unitary Fourier transformation on $\mathbb R^3$. There is an absolute constant $C$ such that for every $b\ge1$ and $Q\in H^{-1/2}(\mathbb R^3)$,
$$\int_{|\xi|\le b}\langle\xi\rangle^{-1}\|e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2\,d\xi\le Cb^2\|Q\|_{H^{-1/2}}^2.$$
Consequently, if $t>0$, $L\ge0$ and $a_\xi\in H^{1/2}(\mathbb R^3)$ is any family with $\|a_\xi\|_{H^{1/2}}\le L/t$ for $|\xi|\le b$, its modulated bilinear distributional remainders
$$R(\xi)=\langle e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q,a_\xi\rangle$$
satisfy
$$\left(\int_{|\xi|\le b}\langle\xi\rangle^{-1}|R(\xi)|^2\,d\xi\right)^{1/2}\le C\frac{Lb}{t}\|Q\|_{H^{-1/2}},$$
whenever the scalar family $R$ is measurable. No continuity or derivative bound in $\xi$ is required.
lem-ip-calderon-boundary-trace-quotient-:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.
lem-ip-centered-neumann-sequence-map-and:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1(0)\subset\mathbb R^3$, fix $0<\rho<1$ and $0<m<1<M$, and let $E$ be the closed real subspace of $L^\infty(\Omega)$ consisting of functions vanishing almost everywhere outside $B_\rho(0)$. Set $\mathcal A=\{a\in E:\operatorname*{ess\,inf}(1+a)>m,\ \operatorname*{ess\,sup}(1+a)<M\}$ and $\sigma=1+a$. Choose an orthonormal spherical-harmonic basis $Y_{\ell k}$ of mean-zero $L^2(S^2)$, with $\ell\ge1$ and $1\le k\le2\ell+1$. For each basis current there is a unique weak solution $u_{\sigma,\ell k}\in H^1(\Omega)$ with boundary mean zero such that
$$\int_\Omega\sigma\nabla u_{\sigma,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla v}=\int_{S^2}Y_{\ell k}\overline{\operatorname{Tr}v}\qquad(v\in H^1(\Omega)).$$
The centered sequence
$$G(a):=\big(\operatorname{Tr}(u_{\sigma,\ell k}-u_{1,\ell k})\big)_{\ell,k}$$
belongs to $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$. The map $G:\mathcal A\to Y$ is Fréchet differentiable, and both $G$ and $G'$ are Lipschitz on $\mathcal A$, with constants depending only on $m,M,\rho$ and the ball. Its derivative in direction $h\in E$ is the trace sequence of the unique boundary-mean-zero solutions
$$\int_\Omega\sigma\nabla v_{h,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla w}=-\int_\Omega h\nabla u_{\sigma,\ell k}\cdot\overline{\nabla w}.$$
The uncentered sequence $(\operatorname{Tr}u_{1,\ell k})_{\ell,k}$ does not belong to $Y$. Thus absolute voltage data in this convention lie in an affine translate of $Y$, whereas data differences belong to $Y$. All complex spaces here may be regarded as real Banach spaces when taking derivatives with respect to real conductivities.
lem-ip-logarithmic-index-conjugate-and-p:
## Statement

Fix $C,\nu>0$ and $0<t_0<e^{-(\nu+1)}$. Define $\psi(0)=0$, $\psi(t)=C[\log(1/t)]^{-\nu}$ for $0<t\le t_0$, and $\psi(t)=\psi(t_0)$ for $t>t_0$. Then $\psi$ is continuous, nondecreasing and concave, and
$$H(q):=\sup_{t\ge0}(\psi(t)-qt)\sim C(\log q)^{-\nu}\qquad(q\to\infty).$$
For each fixed $c>0$, one consequently has $H(cq)/H(q)\to1$. For $p>0$, fixed $D,a,C_*>0$ and nonnegative errors satisfying
$$S_\delta+a\alpha e_\delta\le D\delta^p+\alpha\psi(C_*S_\delta),$$
the balanced choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^p[\log(1/\delta)]^\nu$ gives
$$e_\delta=O([\log(1/\delta)]^{-\nu}),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^p).$$
For a pure-power choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^k$ with $0<k<p$, the same error rate follows, with residual bound $S_\delta=O(\delta^k[\log(1/\delta)]^{-\nu})$. No assertion for $k=p$ is made. If $e_\delta=\frac12\|u_\delta-u^\dagger\|^2$, the corresponding norm rate has exponent $\nu/2$.
lem-ip-collared-liouville-potential-and-:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $5/2<s<7/2$, $0<\rho<1$, $0<m<1<M$ and $A>0$. Suppose $\sigma_j=1+a_j$ on $\mathbb R^3$, where $a_j$ is real, supported in $\overline{B_\rho}$, $\|a_j\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^3)}\le A$, and $m\le\sigma_j\le M$, for $j=1,2$. Then $g_j=\sqrt{\sigma_j}$ and $\log g_j$ belong to $C^1$, with $g_j-1,\log g_j\in H^s(\mathbb R^3)$ supported in $\overline{B_\rho}$ and uniformly bounded in $H^s$ and $C^1$. The real Liouville potentials
$$q_j=g_j^{-1}\Delta g_j$$
belong to $H^{s-2}(\mathbb R^3)$, have support in $\overline{B_\rho}$, and have norms bounded in terms of $s,\rho,m,M,A$. Moreover,
$$\|\sigma_1-\sigma_2\|_{H^1(\mathbb R^3)}\le C\|q_1-q_2\|_{H^{-1}(\mathbb R^3)},$$
with the same dependence. In particular the right side may be replaced by $C\|q_1-q_2\|_{H^{-1/2}}$ when that stronger norm is used. The Fourier and intrinsic norms for collared variations are those of the collared Sobolev source-functional lemma.
lem-ip-logarithmic-endpoint-under-effect:
## Statement

Fix $p,\nu,a,C_*,C>0$ and let $\psi$ be a continuous nondecreasing concave source index with $\psi(0)=0$. Suppose its conjugate $H(q)=\sup_{t\ge0}(\psi(t)-qt)$ satisfies $H(q)\le C(\log q)^{-\nu}$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Let $\delta\downarrow0$ be a nominal parameter, and put $L_\delta=\log(1/\delta)$. Suppose nonnegative errors satisfy
$$S_\delta+a\alpha_\delta e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha_\delta\psi(C_*S_\delta),\qquad \alpha_\delta\asymp\delta^p,\qquad d_\delta=O(\delta^pL_\delta^{-\nu}).$$
Then
$$e_\delta=O(L_\delta^{-\nu}),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^pL_\delta^{-\nu}).$$
For the joint objective estimate with actual data noise $\varepsilon_\delta=\|y^\delta-y\|$, the hypothesis on $d_\delta$ is supplied by $2\varepsilon_\delta^p+\eta_\delta=O(\delta^pL_\delta^{-\nu})$. This condition explicitly strengthens the usual nominal bound $\varepsilon_\delta\le\delta$, $\eta_\delta=O(\delta^p)$ at the endpoint. If $e_\delta=\frac12\|u_\delta-u^\dagger\|^2$, the norm rate is $O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$.

The universal assertion that $\alpha\asymp\delta^2$ yields a vanishing norm error for every deterministic noise family bounded by $\delta$ is false, even for an exact quadratic Tikhonov minimizer and a truth satisfying every nonnegative variational source inequality: on real $\ell^2$, take $Ke_j=j^{-1}e_j$, $x^\dagger=0$, $y^{\delta_j}=\delta_j e_j$, $\delta_j=1/j$, $\alpha_j=\delta_j^2$, and objective $\|Kx-y^{\delta_j}\|^2+\frac{\alpha_j}{2}\|x\|^2$. Its unique minimizer is $2e_j/3$. This counterexample refutes the universal abstract endpoint assertion; it makes no assertion that these data arise from an EIT conductivity map.
lem-ip-centered-ntd-cgo-identity-and-mod:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, and let $\sigma_j=1+a_j$ be positive real conductivities with $a_j$ supported in $\overline{B_\rho}$, $\|a_j\|_{H^s}\le A$, $5/2<s<7/2$, $0<\rho<1$, and $m\le\sigma_j\le M$, for fixed positive bounds. Put $g_j=\sqrt{\sigma_j}$, $q_j=g_j^{-1}\Delta g_j$, $Q=q_1-q_2$, and $N=\|Q\|_{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb R^3)}$. Let $\mathscr N_j$ be the boundary-mean-zero Neumann-to-Dirichlet map for $\sigma_j$ on $L^2_0(S^2)$, and define the actual data difference by the centered voltage sequences
$$\delta=\left(\sum_{\ell\ge1}\sum_{k=1}^{2\ell+1}\|(\mathscr N_1-\mathscr N_2)Y_{\ell k}\|_{L^2(S^2)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
This quantity is finite. If $U_j=e^{i\zeta_j\cdot x}(1+r_j)$ are the solutions from the positive-Sobolev CGO lemma, then
$$\int_\Omega Q U_1U_2\,dx=\int_{S^2}f_1(\mathscr N_2-\mathscr N_1)f_2\,dS,\qquad f_j=\partial_\nu U_j\big|_{S^2},$$
and the fluxes $f_j$ have mean zero. The boundary pairing is bilinear, without complex conjugation. In particular, there are $C,T>0$ depending only on the fixed class such that for $t\ge T$ and $|\xi|\le t$ one can choose null phases with $\zeta_1+\zeta_2=-\xi$, $|\zeta_j|=\sqrt2t$, and obtain the rigorous estimate
$$|\widehat Q(\xi)|\le C\delta e^{Ct}+C\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}t^{-1}N.$$
The factor $\langle\xi\rangle^{1/2}$ is part of this conclusion; this lemma does not assert the sharper stability estimate that would follow from dropping it.

def-ip-differential-range-invariance:
## Definition

Let $X$, $Y$, and $Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be nonempty, let $x_0\in U$, and let $F:U\to Y$ be a map. A **differential range-invariance factorization at $x_0$ on $U$** consists of a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$ and a map $r:U\to Z$ such that

$$F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)\qquad(x\in U).$$

Thus every data increment lies in the range of the fixed operator $K$. The factorization alone does not assert that $K$ is injective, that $r$ is unique, or that a tangential-cone inequality holds. If $U$ is open and $F$ and $r$ are Fréchet differentiable, differentiating this identity gives $F'(x)=Kr'(x)$ at every $x\in U$; no converse is asserted without further hypotheses.
lem-ip-sharp-centered-eit-hone-logarithm:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Fix $5/2<s<7/2$, $0<\rho<1$, $0<m<1<M$ and $A>0$. Let $\sigma_j=1+a_j$ be real conductivities on $\mathbb R^3$, with $a_j$ supported in $\overline{B_\rho}$, $\|a_j\|_{H^s}\le A$, and $m\le\sigma_j\le M$, for $j=1,2$. Let $\mathscr N_j$ be their boundary-mean-zero NtD maps on $S^2=\partial B_1$, and let
$$\delta=\left(\sum_{\ell\ge1}\sum_{k=1}^{2\ell+1}\|(\mathscr N_1-\mathscr N_2)Y_{\ell k}\|_{L^2(S^2)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
Then there is $C>0$ depending only on $s,\rho,m,M,A$ such that
$$\|\sigma_1-\sigma_2\|_{H^1(\mathbb R^3)}\le C\left[\log(3+\delta^{-1})\right]^{-(s-3/2)}\qquad(\delta>0).$$
If $\delta=0$, the conductivities are equal. The zero-noise modulus is therefore defined to be zero. Restricting the left side to $B_1$ gives the same $H^1$ norm because the difference is supported in $\overline{B_\rho}$.
def-ip-relaxed-range-invariance-objectiv:
## Definition

Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D\subseteq X$ contain $X_0$ and a nonempty set $U$. Fix $x_0\in X_0\cap U$, a map $F:D\to Y$, a bounded linear map $K:Z\to Y$, and a map $r:D\to Z$ such that $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for every $x\in D$. Assume that $r|_U$ is a bijection from $U$ onto a set $\widetilde U\subseteq Z$, and that $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in X_0\cap D$ for every $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$ admitted below. Here $I$ is the identity on $X$ and $P:X\to X$ is a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be a proper convex regularizer, let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ be a nonnegative penalty, and let $Q:Z\times Z\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$. For $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, set

$$\mathcal R(\widehat r):=\check R\big((I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\big)+R_P\big(Pr^{-1}(\widehat r)\big).$$

For $p\in[1,\infty)$, data $y^\delta\in Y$, and parameters $\alpha,\beta>0$, the **joint relaxed objective** is

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p+\|Px\|_X^p,\qquad (\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U.$$

The joint source-condition objective takes $R_P=0$. The term $\beta Q(r(x),\widehat r)^p$ ties the relaxed range variable to the physical variable, while $\|Px\|_X^p$ penalizes the component outside $X_0$.

If $r$ is Gâteaux differentiable at a current iterate $x_n\in U$, the **frozen-Newton objective** with parameters $\alpha_n,\beta_n>0$ is

$$\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r,x):=\|K\widehat r+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha_n\mathcal R(\widehat r)+\beta_n Q\big(r(x_n)+r'(x_n)(x-x_n),\widehat r\big)^p+\|Px\|_X^p.$$

Here $r'(x_n)$ is the bounded linear Gâteaux derivative used to form the affine range proxy; no minimizer existence or uniqueness is part of either definition.
lem-ip-joint-range-invariance-vsc-estima:
## Statement

Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, $X_0\subseteq X$ a closed linear subspace, $D\subseteq X$ a domain containing $X_0$ and $U$, and $x_0\in U\cap X_0$. Let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, with $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ bijective and $r$ Lipschitz with constant $L_r$ on $D$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection such that $P|_{X_0}=0$, $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$, and $P(x_0)=P(x^\dagger)=0$ for an exact solution $x^\dagger\in U\cap X_0$; put $y:=F(x^\dagger)$. Assume the projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $D\cap X_0$ for all admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)\subseteq X_0^*$, and suppose that for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$, $b\in[0,1)$, and continuous nondecreasing concave $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger)+\psi\big(\|F(\check x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\big)$$

holds whenever $\check x\in D\cap X_0$ and $\check R(\check x)\le R_0$, where $D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x,x^\dagger):=\check R(\check x)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,\check x-x^\dagger\rangle$. Set $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Let $Q:\widetilde U\times\widetilde U\to[0,\infty]$ satisfy $Q(a,b)=Q(b,a)$ and $Q(a,b)=0$ exactly when $a=b$, and assume there is a constant $C_Q\ge0$ such that

$$\|P(r^{-1}(a))-P(r^{-1}(b))\|_X\le C_Q Q(a,b)\qquad(a,b\in\widetilde U).$$

For $\delta>0$, let $y^\delta\in Y$ satisfy $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$. Let $\alpha,\beta>0$, $C_\eta\ge0$, and let $(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\in\widetilde U\times U$ be an $\eta_\delta$-minimizer of the joint objective, meaning

$$\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r_\delta,x_\delta)\le\mathcal J_{\alpha,\beta}^\delta(\widehat r,x)+\eta_\delta\qquad((\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U),\qquad 0\le\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p.$$

Assume $\check x_\delta:=(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r_\delta)$ lies in the stated VSC sublevel. Define

$$s_\delta:=2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y^p+\beta Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)^p+\|Px_\delta\|_X^p,\qquad e_\delta:=D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger),$$

and

$$C_*:=2^{2p-2}\max\left\{1,\|K\|^pL_r^p,\frac{\|K\|^pL_r^pC_Q^p}{\beta}\right\},\qquad d_\delta:=(2+C_\eta)\delta^p.$$

Then

$$s_\delta+(1-b)\alpha e_\delta\le d_\delta+\alpha\psi(C_*s_\delta).$$
lem-ip-frozen-newton-one-step-error-recu:
## Statement

Let $1\le p<\infty$. Let $X,Y,Z$ be real Banach spaces, let $X_0$ be a closed linear subspace of $X$, and let $D,U\subseteq X$. Let $x_0,x^\dagger\in D\cap U\cap X_0$, let $F:D\to Y$, $K\in\mathcal L(Z,Y)$, and $r:D\to Z$ satisfy $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ for all $x\in D$. Assume $r|_U:U\to\widetilde U$ is a bijection, $r$ is Lipschitz on $D$ with constant $L_r$, and $r$ has bounded linear Gâteaux derivatives on $U$. Let $P:X\to X$ be a bounded linear projection with $P^2=P$, $P|_{X_0}=0$, and $(I-P)(X)\subseteq X_0$. Assume $P(x^\dagger)=0$ and $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)\in D\cap X_0$ for each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$.

Let $\check R:X_0\to[0,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial\check R(x^\dagger)$, and write

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger):=\check R(z)-\check R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}.$$

Suppose that, on the stated sublevel $\check R(z)\le R_0$, the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,z-x^\dagger\rangle_{X_0^*,X_0}\le bD_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(z,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(z)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)$$

holds for some $R_0\ge\check R(x^\dagger)$ and $0\le b<1$. Assume that $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous, nondecreasing and concave, with $\psi(0)=0$, and that for a constant $C_\psi>0$,

$$\psi(a+b)\le C_\psi\bigl(\psi(a)+\psi(b)\bigr)\qquad(a,b\ge0).$$

Let $H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$, and assume the values of $H$ used below are finite. Let $\gamma>C_\psi$, $C_P\ge2^{p-1}\|K\|^pL_r^p$, and $\widetilde C_Q>0$. Let $R_P:P(X)\to[0,+\infty]$ satisfy $R_P(0)=0$ and

$$R_P(z)\ge\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_X^p)\qquad(z\in P(X)).$$

For each admitted $\widehat r\in\widetilde U$, put $u(\widehat r):=r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ and $\check x(\widehat r):=(I-P)u(\widehat r)$. Assume the compatibility bound

$$\|\widehat r-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\le\widetilde C_Q\left(D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x(\widehat r),x^\dagger)+\psi(C_P\|Pu(\widehat r)\|_X^p)\right).$$

Choose $c_{\beta\alpha}>0$ with $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and set

$$m:=\min\{1-b,\gamma-C_\psi\},\quad a:=2^{1-p},\quad \lambda:=2^{1-p},\quad t:=2^{2-2p}-2^{p-1}c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad v:=(1+2^{p-1})c_{\rm tcr}^p,\quad \overline C:=C_\psi 2^{2p-2}.$$

Assume $0<c_{\rm tcr}<1$ and $t>0$, and for all $x_1,x_2\in U$ assume

$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le c_{\rm tcr}\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z.$$

Assume the candidate projected point satisfies $\check R(\check x(\widehat r_{n+1}))\le R_0$.

Let $Q(a,b):=\|a-b\|_Z$. Fix $\delta>0$, $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y\le\delta$, and $\alpha_n>0$, with $\beta_n:=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$. Suppose $(\widehat r_{n+1},x_{n+1})\in\widetilde U\times U$ satisfies, for some $\eta_n\ge0$,

$$\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r_{n+1},x_{n+1})\le\mathcal J_n^\delta(\widehat r,x)+\eta_n\qquad((\widehat r,x)\in\widetilde U\times U),$$

where $\mathcal J_n^\delta$ is the frozen objective in the Joint and frozen-Newton objectives definition, with regularizer $\mathcal R(\widehat r)=\check R(\check x(\widehat r))+R_P(Pu(\widehat r))$ and distance $Q$.

Define

$$E_{n+1}:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\left(\lambda\|\widehat r_{n+1}-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+t\|r(x_{n+1})-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\right),$$

$$S_{n+1}:=\frac{1}{C_\psi}\left(2^{1-p}\|K(\widehat r_{n+1}-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y^p+\|Px_{n+1}\|_X^p\right),$$

and

$$d_n:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\alpha_n v\|r(x_n)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+\frac{2\delta^p+\eta_n}{C_\psi}.$$

Then

$$S_{n+1}+\alpha_nE_{n+1}\le d_n+\alpha_n\psi(\overline C S_{n+1}).$$

Consequently,

$$E_{n+1}\le\frac{d_n}{\alpha_n}+H\!\left(\frac{1}{\overline C\alpha_n}\right),\qquad S_{n+1}\le2\left(d_n+\alpha_nH\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\alpha_n}\right)\right).$$
lem-ip-eit-centered-range-invariance-vsc:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, $0<\rho<1$, $0<m<1<M$, and $5/2<s_1<7/2$. Use the exact intrinsic $H^{s_1}(\Omega)$ Hilbert norm from the collared source-functional lemma, and put
$$V=\{a\in H^{s_1}(\Omega;\mathbb R):a=0\text{ a.e. on }\Omega\setminus B_\rho\},\qquad \mathcal C=\{\sigma\in1+V:m\le\sigma\le M\}.$$
Let $\sigma_0,\sigma^\dagger\in\mathcal C$, and assume $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_1<s_2<2s_1-1$. Set $a^\dagger=\sigma^\dagger-\sigma_0$, and choose $R>\|a^\dagger\|_V$. Write $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2;\mathbb C))$ for the centered mean-zero Neumann voltage sequence space, regarded as a real Hilbert space, and give $X=Z=V\times Y$ the sum norm. Let $X_0=V\times\{0\}$, $D=X$, $x_0=(0,0)$ and $P(a,z)=(0,z)$.

There is a globally Lipschitz, continuously Fréchet differentiable map $\Gamma:V\to Y$ with globally Lipschitz derivative, agreeing for $\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C$ with the centered physical observation $((\mathscr N_{\sigma_0+a}-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k})_{\ell,k}$. Define
$$T(a)=\Gamma(a)-\Gamma(0)-\Gamma'(0)a,\quad r(a,z)=(a,z+T(a)),\quad K(a,b)=\Gamma'(0)a+b,\quad F(a,z)=\Gamma(a)+z.$$
Then $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, $r$ and its inverse $r^{-1}(a,b)=(a,b-T(a))$ are globally Lipschitz, and these facts hold on the admitted set
$$U=\{(a,z):\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C,\ \|a\|_V<R,\ \|z\|_Y<R\}.$$
The projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $U\cap X_0$ for $\widehat r\in r(U)$.

On the ambient linear space $V$ define the proper convex regularizer
$$\check R(a)=\tfrac12\|\sigma_0+a\|_{s_1,\Omega}^2+I_{\mathcal C}(\sigma_0+a),$$
where the indicator is zero on $\mathcal C$ and $+\infty$ elsewhere. On every admitted physical coefficient this is exactly the original quadratic Sobolev penalty. The functional $\xi^\dagger(v)=(\sigma^\dagger,v)_{s_1,\Omega}$ is a subgradient at $a^\dagger$, and its Bregman distance on $\mathcal C-\sigma_0$ is exactly $\frac12\|a-a^\dagger\|_V^2$. On every fixed sublevel containing the truth, the VSC holds with $b=3/4$ and a continuous nondecreasing concave truncated logarithmic index
$$\psi(u)=C[\log(1/u)]^{-\nu}\quad(0<u\le u_0),\qquad \psi(0)=0,\qquad \nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},$$
continued constantly above a sufficiently small $u_0>0$. Its subadditivity constant may be taken as $C_\psi=1$.

Put $L_T=\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ and let $L=\operatorname{Lip}(\Gamma')$. For $Q(\widehat r,\widehat r')=\|\widehat r-\widehat r'\|_Z$, the projection-coupling constant may be taken as $1+L_T$, and
$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le LR\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z\qquad(x_1,x_2\in U).$$
For the frozen method choose $C_P\ge2\|K\|^2\operatorname{Lip}(r)^2$, $\gamma>1$ and $R_P(z)=\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_Y^2)$. Then the required compatibility bound holds with
$$\widetilde C_Q=\max\left\{4(1+L_T)^2,\frac{2R^2}{\psi(C_PR^2)}\right\}.$$
In particular, the structural hypotheses of the joint and frozen one-step estimates hold with $p=2$, the displayed exact regularizer, $R_P=0$ for the joint method, and the displayed $R_P$ for the frozen method. For frozen rates additionally require $LR<c_{\rm tcr}<1/\sqrt{20}$, choose $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1/4,\gamma-1\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and use the remaining parameter, tolerance and stopping conditions of the frozen rate theorem. This small-neighborhood hypothesis is local around the chosen initial conductivity; it restricts neither the stated Besov truth class nor its logarithmic exponent.
thm-ip-joint-regularization-rate-under-r:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma, with the same notation, with fixed $\beta>0$, and with $R_P=0$ in the joint objective. Define

$$H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}\bigl(\psi(s)-qs\bigr)\qquad(q>0),\quad \rho_\delta:=H\!\left(\frac{1}{C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right).$$

Assume $H(1/(C_*\alpha(\delta)))$ and $H(1/(2C_*\alpha(\delta)))$ are finite, $\alpha(\delta)\to0$, $\rho_\delta\to0$, $\eta_\delta\le C_\eta\delta^p$, and there are constants $c_-,c_+,C_H>0$ independent of $\delta$ such that

$$c_-\delta^p\le\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p,\qquad H\!\left(\frac{1}{2C_*\alpha(\delta)}\right)\le C_H\rho_\delta.$$

Then the approximate joint reconstructions satisfy, as $\delta\downarrow0$,

$$D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(\check x_\delta,x^\dagger)=O(\rho_\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^p),$$

where $S_\delta$ is the scalar residual, coupling, and projection error defined in the joint range-invariance VSC estimate lemma. In particular,

$$\|K(\widehat r_\delta-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y=O(\delta),\quad \|Px_\delta\|_X=O(\delta),\quad Q(r(x_\delta),\widehat r_\delta)=O(\delta),$$

and the data residual $\|K\widehat r_\delta+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y$ is $O(\delta)$.

For the following three-dimensional EIT specialization, assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, let the known background be $1$ outside $B_\rho\Subset B_1$, and impose fixed bounds $0<m<1<M$ and $m\le\sigma\le M$. Let $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, use the intrinsic quadratic penalty $\frac12\|\sigma\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}^2$ on this admissible class, and let $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ with $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. The Sobolev norm is the exact intrinsic Hilbert norm in the EIT compatibility lemma. Use centered mean-zero Neumann voltage data $(\mathscr N_\sigma-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k}$ in $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$, its observation-augmentation range coordinates, and admitted approximate joint minimizers in the set $U$ specified by that lemma. The artificial voltage is $z\in Y$ and the projection is $P(\sigma-\sigma_0,z)=(0,z)$. Put

$$\nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},\qquad L_\delta=\log(1/\delta).$$

For fixed $\beta>0$, noise bounded by $\delta$, and $\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2)$, the balanced choice $\alpha\asymp\delta^2L_\delta^\nu$ gives

$$\|\sigma_\delta-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}=O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2}),\qquad \|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad S_\delta=O(\delta^2).$$

Every pure power $\alpha\asymp\delta^k$ with $0<k<2$ gives the same conductivity norm rate and $S_\delta=O(\delta^kL_\delta^{-\nu})$, hence $\|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta^{k/2}L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$. At the nominal endpoint $\alpha\asymp\delta^2$, the same conductivity norm rate holds under the explicit actual-noise and tolerance condition

$$2\|y^\delta-y\|_Y^2+\eta_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu});$$

then $S_\delta=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu})$ and $\|z_\delta\|_Y=O(\delta L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$. In each case the coupling distance and relaxed data residual have order $O(\sqrt{S_\delta}+\|y^\delta-y\|_Y)$. In particular the sum of the conductivity norm error and the artificial-voltage norm is $O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2})$ in all three stated regimes.
thm-ip-frozen-newton-rate-under-range-in:
## Statement

Assume the structural hypotheses of the frozen Newton one-step error lemma hold with fixed constants and notation. Let the initial pair be $(\widehat r_0,x_0)\in\widetilde U\times U$, where $x_0$ is the basepoint from the range-invariance factorization. At step $n\ge1$, freeze the objective at the previous iterate $x_{n-1}$, use parameters $\alpha_n$ and $\beta_n=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$, and let $(\widehat r_n,x_n)$ satisfy the resulting approximate-minimum inequality. Let $E_n$ and $S_n$ be the error and residual quantities from the one-step lemma for this step, with its input iterate relabeled $x_{n-1}$ and output iterate relabeled $x_n$. Define $E_0:=\frac{c_{\beta\alpha}}{C_\psi}\bigl(\lambda\|\widehat r_0-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+t\|r(x_0)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p\bigr)$. The parameter sequence $(\alpha_n)_{n\ge1}$ and the associated $h_n,\rho_n$ are fixed independently of $\delta$. Write

$$H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs),\quad h_n:=H\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\alpha_n}\right),\quad \rho_n:=\alpha_n h_n,\quad q:=\frac{v}{t},$$

where $t,v,\overline C$ are as in that lemma. Let $\alpha_n>0$ decrease strictly to zero, suppose $h_n$ is finite and positive, $\rho_n$ decreases strictly to zero, and assume for some $C_H\ge1$ that

$$h_n\le C_Hh_{n+1}\quad(n\ge1),\qquad qC_H<1.$$

Assume each step through $N$ satisfies the one-step lemma, has tolerance $\eta_n\le C_\eta\rho_n$, and the initial error $E_0$ is finite. Assume also that for every sufficiently small $\delta>0$ there is an index $N=N(\delta)\ge2$ such that

$$\rho_N\ge\tau\delta^p,\qquad \rho_N\le M\tau\delta^p,\qquad \rho_n\ge\tau\delta^p\quad(1\le n\le N),$$

for constants $\tau,M>0$ independent of $\delta$. This bounded crossing condition is satisfied, for example, if $N$ is the last index with $\rho_N\ge\tau\delta^p$ and $\rho_n/\rho_{n+1}\le M$ for all $n$.

Then the stopping iterate $(\widehat r_N,x_N)$ satisfies

$$E_N=O(h_N),\qquad S_N=O(\delta^p),$$

and therefore

$$\|\widehat r_N-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p+\|r(x_N)-r(x^\dagger)\|_Z^p=O(h_N),$$

$$\|K(\widehat r_N-r(x^\dagger))\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad \|Px_N\|_X=O(\delta),\qquad \|K\widehat r_N+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta).$$

If $\Phi(a):=aH(1/(2\overline C a))$ has a strictly increasing inverse $\phi$ on the relevant range, then

$$h_N\le H\!\left(\frac{1}{2\overline C\,\phi(M\tau\delta^p)}\right),$$

which gives the corresponding source-index rate for the range-variable and nonlinear-range errors.

For the following three-dimensional EIT specialization, assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, let the known conductivity be $1$ outside $B_\rho\Subset B_1$, impose fixed positive upper and lower conductivity bounds, use the exact intrinsic quadratic $H^{s_1}(\Omega)$ penalty with $s_1\in(5/2,7/2)$, and assume $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_2\in(s_1,2s_1-1)$. Use the centered mean-zero Neumann voltage map in $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2))$ and the explicit observation augmentation, admitted neighborhood $U$, penalty $R_P$, and linked-parameter constants in the EIT compatibility lemma. Choose the initial conductivity sufficiently close to the truth that its radius condition $LR<c_{\rm tcr}<1/\sqrt{20}$ holds, and choose a fixed initial range variable in $r(U)$, independently of noise. Put

$$\nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},\qquad L_\delta=\log(1/\delta).$$

Take a fixed geometric parameter sequence, starting sufficiently far down its tail that the conjugate growth condition above holds, set $\beta_n=c_{\beta\alpha}\alpha_n$, and use admitted approximate steps with $\eta_n\le C_\eta\rho_n$. For a positive target $w_\delta$, stop at the last index $N$ with $\rho_N\ge\tau w_\delta$. If the actual squared data noise is $O(w_\delta)$, then

$$\|\sigma_N-\sigma^\dagger\|_{H^{s_1}(\Omega)}=O(L_\delta^{-\nu/2}),\qquad \|z_N\|_Y=O(\sqrt{w_\delta}),\qquad \|K\widehat r_N+F(x_0)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\sqrt{w_\delta})$$

in each of the following regimes: $w_\delta=\delta^2$ for the balanced choice $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^2L_\delta^\nu$ and ordinary noise bounded by $\delta$; $w_\delta=\delta^kL_\delta^{-\nu}$ for every $0<k<2$, giving $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^k$ under the same ordinary noise bound; and $w_\delta=\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu}$ for the nominal endpoint $\alpha_N\asymp\delta^2$, under the explicit stronger actual-noise condition $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y^2=O(\delta^2L_\delta^{-\nu})$. All tolerances remain bounded by $C_\eta\rho_n$ through the stopping index. Thus the total conductivity and artificial-voltage norm error has logarithmic exponent $\nu/2$ in every stated regime.
